text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
- CSU parliamentary leader Michael Glos says party gathering in Wildbad Kreuth will focus on CSU issues -- foreigners, tax reform, pensions and advice for the FDP
- German President Roman Herzog to be honoured with Karlspreis in Aachen in May.

- Chancellor Helmut Kohl confirms that when government moves to Berlin the Chancellery will be temporarily headquarted in Council of Ministers' building. Says government will move to Berlin as soon as parliament moves to Berlin.
- PDS press spokesman Harno Harnisch admits he had earlier contacts to East German security police (Stasi).
- Frankfurt prosecutors in Frankfurt have started probes against Hesse state Finance Ministry officials on suspicion of fraud in connection with dividend stripping.
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel in favour of smaller cuts in tax breaks for commuters who drive cars to work.
- Unemployent in December believed to have jumped sharply to more than 4.1 million, according to survey of economists.
- IG Medien union warns of possible strike in printing industry.
- Unemployment expected to rise to 4.1 million in December, analysts say.
- Waigel wants to tax pension payments
- CDU parliamentary leader Wolfgang Schaeuble tells Stern magazine he feels able to one day become Chancellor.
- Greens demand SPD announce coaltion intentions for 1998 election. Parliamentary leader Joschka Fischer says Greens and SPD need to work together to oust Kohl.
- German job market hit by cold shock. Hard winter and weak economy lead to rise in jobless totals.
